title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-03-23
content:
Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-03-23
Owner: Priya Patel
Team: eng-infrastructure
Status: In review

Summary:
- This week focused on short-term capacity smoothing for hosted API peak traffic, rolling kernel/driver updates in eu-west-1, and validating the new batching config for long-context models.
- No customer-facing outages; one internal degradation (short-term increased latency) due to a thermal mitigation event in us-west-2 that auto-evacuated a single rack.
- Preparing procurement and onboarding plan for +240 A100 GPUs (Q2 sprint) to address projected Dedicated and Hosted demand.

Fleet snapshot (2026-03-23):
- Total GPUs online: 1,120 (across all regions).
- Average utilization (7d): 68% global; peak sustained during US business hours 84%.
- Region breakdown:
  - us-west-2: 420 GPUs, avg util 72%, incidented rack under monitoring (see incidents).
  - us-east-1: 300 GPUs, avg util 77%, higher preemption risk on spot-backed capacity (working with cloud PM).
  - eu-west-1: 260 GPUs, avg util 63%, migrations ongoing for the driver update rollout.
  - ap-southeast-1: 140 GPUs, avg util 52%, headroom intentionally reserved for APAC pilot customers.

Capacity and demand planning:
- Short-term (next 4 weeks): expect a ~12% increase in hosted API token volume due to two PLG campaigns. We recommend enabling 20% burst capacity on Dedicated pools for low-latency tiers to avoid throttling.
- Mid-term (Q2): procurement plan approved for +240 A100 GPUs. Target arrival and racking window: 2026-05-10 -> 2026-05-24. Sequencing will prioritize us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for latency-sensitive workloads.
- Long-term (Q3 prep): begin evaluation of RTX-grade nodes for cost-sensitive embedding workloads and a small on-prem pilot for a Private customer (gov-regulated).

Recent changes / deployments:
- Batching config v1.4 deployed to serving pools in eu-west-1 (canary -> 25% -> 100%). Observed a 9% reduction in per-token cost for typical chat workloads with <1% tail latency increase.
- Kernel/driver update (CUDA 12.x + NCCL minor) rolled to 40% of eu-west-1; rollout paused after a node-level thermal event surfaced in canary. Root cause tied to BIOS firmware mismatch; remediation plan in place.
- KV cache invalidation fix (PR #487) merged; reduces cache thrashing for multi-turn chat on long-context models.

Incidents / Alerts:
- 2026-03-21 us-west-2 thermal mitigation (internal-only): one rack experienced elevated temps; cooling PDU kicked in and nodes were evacuated. Impact: short-term tail latency spike (~2-3 minutes) for some Hosted API requests routed to that rack before automated failover completed. No customer-facing errors logged.
  - Action taken: rack moved to maintenance, nodes inspected, one PSU replaced. Cooling thresholds adjusted.
  - Follow-up: SREs to run a 72-hour thermal soak test on neighboring racks (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-28).

Blockers / Risks:
- Spot preemption volatility in us-east-1 is higher than forecasted; risk to Dedicated burst capacity for cost-optimized pools. Mitigation: increase reserved-base for critical tiers; implement faster graceful degradation fallback to smaller model variants. (Owner: Alex Moreno)
- Driver/firmware heterogeneity across older racks causing stalled driver rollouts; need inventory reconciliation and firmware flash plan. (Owner: Ethan Chen)

Upcoming milestones & calendar:
- 2026-03-30: Finalize Dedicated burst policy and quota increase for Hosted PLG surge window.
- 2026-04-07: Complete eu-west-1 driver rollout (pending firmware remediation).
- 2026-05-10: Begin racking new A100 nodes (phase 1).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Alex Moreno: Define fallback routing policy for spot preemptions and update runbooks (due 2026-03-29).
- Ethan Chen: Produce firmware inventory report and flash schedule for heterogeneous racks (due 2026-03-31).
- Liam O'Connor: Run 72-hour thermal soak and report metrics, include cooling PDU logs (due 2026-03-28).
- Maya Rodriguez: Coordinate procurement intake with finance and ops for A100 order; confirm lead times and shipping SLA (due 2026-03-26).
- Priya Patel (owner): Draft capacity-commitment memo for Sales to align on Q2 Dedicated opens (due 2026-03-27).

Notes from daily standups this week (high level):
- Mon: Focus on driver rollout gating; SRE flagged two racks with out-of-date firmware.
- Tue: Batching config canary showed reduced cost; teams asked to validate for long-context evals.
- Wed: us-west-2 thermal event and immediate evacuation; incident response runbook executed but timing improvements noted.
- Thu: Procurement details finalized for A100 order; finance signoff pending.
- Fri: Planning for surge window; discussed augmenting canary traffic generator to better emulate PLG traffic patterns.

Notes / open questions for leadership:
- Approve 20% burst capacity budget for April PLG surge? Finance asks for expected incremental monthly spend estimate (we'll provide a cost delta by 2026-03-25).
- Confirm priority regions for new A100 staging (us-west-2 vs eu-west-1) given Sales commitments in EMEA and large US customers.

Appendices / data points (quick):
- 7-day rolling average token volume change: +11.8% week-over-week.
- Current average per-token infra cost (estimate): $0.00042/token (global weighted average).
- Pending JIRA tickets referenced: INFRA-342 (driver rollout), INFRA-359 (procurement intake), INFRA-373 (thermal mitigation RCA).

If you want a deeper breakdown (per-queue latency heatmaps, per-account capacity reservations, or the firmware inventory CSV) I can attach in next update or link to the Confluence inventory page.

-- Priya Patel
